# Two coded-helper embeddings: exact global packing obstruction

**Status: scoped negative result. No new exponent or selected-bound change.**

The one-helper packet construction in [PR781](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/781)
survives integration into two historical native provider chains. Its complete
helper bill defeats the local saving. This package retains four explicit native
circuits and proves that every nonempty mixture of these circuits with the
original providers exceeds PR626's complex moment budget, even after removing
the scheduling and physical-family restrictions from the owner problem.

The claim concerns these four circuits and the stated whole-helper hosting
model. It does not rule out other coded circuits, frame assignments, helper
sharing contracts, dispatches or geometries. PR626 is the historical comparison;
the selected result at this package's base commit is PR799.

## Reproduce

From the repository root, using Python 3.11+ and its standard library:

```sh
python -B research/complex-coded-helper-global-screen/verify.py
```

Expected status: `PASS_SCOPED_INTEGER_PACKING_OBSTRUCTION`. To retain the native
words after transport, detailed audit receipts, failure controls and derived
budget data, append `--out /path/to/a/new/directory`. An existing output
directory is rejected. The default uses a temporary directory.

The command freshly replays all four committed words on every arbitrary-dirt
column in both orientations, recounts their native frame costs and helper
widths, and checks the exact certificate. It rejects five circuit mutations and
three mathematical mutations. A different gzip header and compression level
must reproduce the same complete mathematical receipt. Source archives retain
exact input hashes; generated words use hashes of their decompressed payloads.

The inherited auditor uses assertions. It runs in a separate interpreter with
assertions enabled, including when the parent uses `-O` or inherits
`PYTHONOPTIMIZE`. New certificate guards use explicit exceptions.

Validation passed on Windows with Python 3.13.5 and optimized Python 3.14.4
(also with `PYTHONOPTIMIZE=2` set). The retained mathematical results agree.
No repository-wide suite, Linux CI or full selected-frontier replay is claimed.

This is replay of retained explicit circuits, not a cold reconstruction of their
entire ancestral search. The baseline profile, dispatch and capacity inputs are
pinned to the inherited certificate. The baseline's full phase, controller,
physical-owner and outer-theorem checks are not rerun here.

## What was integrated

The baseline is `research/complex-k492-owner-repair/`, as retained at commit
`66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`. The five inputs used here have identical
bytes at this package's base, `f567884aeb8851b6e794af1184119a3bfbe1e631`.
`SOURCE-PINS.json` identifies them and the PR781 cell at commit
`85f9cfad7708cc3873bd6b32492a618feb336e59`.

Two placements use the same 28-gate coded core, on pair `(6,7)`:

| Placement | Change relative to the R492 provider | Helpers | Columns per orientation |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| positive | Open the positive cell; replace three packet helpers with one coded helper | 490 | 714 |
| negative | Recode the already expanded negative cell; add one coded helper | 493 | 717 |

Each placement is carried through both `ck` and `jp8`. The fresh coded helper is
register 448. It has its own semantic role; it does not inherit an optimization
intended for a removed packet helper. Both variants need eight rank-one dyadic
correction reads at the start of B, after the entry wrappers. Without them the
auditor reconstructs a forbidden zero-frame read from an entering helper.

The positive placement also needs nine tail frame lifts, three cold ends raised
from dimension 4 to 7, and twelve full-frame cleanup corrections. The negative
placement retains the old endpoints and omits the six old frame-regroup edits
on reads that the coded core replaced. These are material costs of integration.
`CONSTRUCTION-RECORD.json` records the core's register bindings and gate indices,
the corrections, final frame raises, and hashes of intermediate discovery words.
Those intermediate words are not required or regenerated by this package.

The final native audits establish exact forward and inverse-transpose endpoints,
arbitrary helper dirt, dyadic primitives, common monotone frames, cold-end cone
conditions, cleanup restoration, and the paid profile. They do not establish
phase lowering, residual adapters or a global owner map for the changed words.
Those later stages cannot rescue a failed lower bound on the required cost.

The resulting per-call changes are the same for `ck` and `jp8`:

| Placement | Delta H1 | Delta H2 | Delta H3 | Delta H4 | Delta H5 | Helper-width change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| positive | +2 | +18 | +8 | -5 | -9 | remove three width-4; add one width-9 |
| negative | -7 | -3 | +2 | +4 | 0 | add one width-9 |

The verifier derives this table from the newly replayed words and the pinned
baseline, rather than taking it as input to the cost proof.

## Fixed budget and favorable relaxation

Keep PR626's 72 calls (8 `ck`, 64 `jp8`), `m = 73`, 7,168 live streams and rank
deficit 2,560. At each call choose its original word, its positive replacement,
or its negative replacement. The two replacements are not composed within a
single call. Provider-independent deltas reduce the choices to 2,700 nonempty
pairs `(p,n)` with `p >= 0`, `n >= 0`, `p+n <= 72`.

The original aggregate local profile is

```text
{1:181536, 2:30016, 3:31104, 4:11520, 5:5040, 6:576, 8:576}.
```

The baseline helper counts and available slot capacities are:

| Helper width | 4 | 5 | 7 | 8 | 9 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Count | 2160 | 3456 | 2848 | 7904 | 19056 |

| Slot capacity | 8 | 16 | 32 | 48 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Count | 5376 | 3584 | 3584 | 3584 |

The capacity inventory is recounted both from the plan's windows (112 ports per
window) and from all 112 native data recipes (8 replicas per port). The two
rank-zero children per port and replica cannot host positive-width helpers.
The original idle profile is `{1:123, 37:1, 48:2215}`. Local plus idle rank mass
is always 520,704.

For the lower bound, discard all time windows, call labels and physical-family
uniqueness restrictions. Each helper still occupies its full audited width in
one capacity slot. All integer multisets of widths fitting a slot are allowed,
including the empty multiset: 1,163 patterns. A pattern with leftover rank `r`
is charged just one idle child of rank `r`. Splitting it could only increase
`sum r^s` for `0 < s < 1`, so this is favorable to the candidate. No feasible
assignment or global circuit is inferred from the relaxation.

## Exact certificate

Use the inherited endpoint

```text
b0 = 65528268492323474503 / 40000000000000000000000,
s = 1 - b0,
phi(r) = r^s - r, with phi(0) = 0.
```

Give capacities `8,16,32,48` the integer scores `6,12,24,37`, and widths
`4,5,7,8,9` the scores `3,3,5,6,7`. For a pattern P in capacity c, define

```text
B(P) = capacity_score(c) - sum width_score(w) * count_P(w).
```

Enumeration checks `B(P) >= 0` for every pattern. The certificate supplies a
negative rational `lambda` and 37 rational potentials `d[0],...,d[36]`, with
`d[0]=0`. The verifier checks, for every pattern and every residue j,

```text
phi(r(P)) >= lambda * B(P),
d[(j+B(P)) mod 37] - d[j] <= phi(r(P)) - lambda * B(P).
```

These are 1,163 scalar inequalities and 43,031 potential inequalities. For any
integer packing, order its slot patterns arbitrarily and telescope the second
inequality from residue zero. Their total score is fixed by the demand:

```text
S = 81984 + 2*p - 7*n.
sum_P phi(r(P)) >= lambda*S + d[S mod 37].
```

If `I` is the fixed leftover rank mass and `H_local` the audited local profile,
every such packing therefore has moment numerator at least

```text
sum_r H_local(r)*r^s + I + lambda*S + d[S mod 37].
```

`exact.py` proves this lower bound strictly exceeds `7168 * 73^s` for every
nonempty mixture. The smallest certified excess is greater than
**0.023249063103**, at `(p,n) = (0,1)`. All child ranks are at most 48, below 73,
so the normalized moment increases with b. Failure at b0 excludes b0 and every
larger saving exponent in this fixed model.

The integer correction matters. Replacing all potentials with zero still
satisfies the pattern inequalities but fails to exclude the single negative
replacement. This is an explicit control, not an assumption of numerical MIP
optimality. A positive control verifies that the inherited *unmodified* global
profile satisfies its own endpoint.

All real-power comparisons use rational intervals. Write `r = 2^k m` with
`1 <= m < 2`; evaluate `log r` using 48 terms of the atanh series, with argument
at most 1/3 and an explicit geometric tail. Bound `exp(-b0 log r)` by its degree
21 and degree 20 alternating polynomials, then round outward at scale `10^30`.
The stored potentials use scale `10^16`. No floating-point result, optimizer,
or shortest-path implementation is trusted by the verifier.

## Search record and limits

The starting experiment was PR781's seed-23 positive cell. This follow-up tried
that placement and the same pair's already expanded negative cell, retaining
the original coded core and pivot. The provider optimizations were ported to
each changed word, repaired where the native audit rejected them, and audited
again. A final greedy search considered legal raises of the 28 coded gates:
one-vector extensions and the maximal common next frame, at most 12 sweeps.
It accepted three raises for each positive word and eight for each negative
word. This is a bounded search, with no claim of frame optimality.

Fractional LP and integer MIP exploration suggested the obstruction. The
37-state potentials were then constructed from the nonnegative reduced costs.
Only the retained exact inequalities are part of the proof. Search stopped when
the exact lower bound excluded all 2,700 mixtures; no phase lowering or global
owner nomination was attempted after that decision.

Related owner-profile results [PR795](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/795)
and [PR850](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/850) concern the
SW4 inventory and establish stronger packing results for that fixed inventory.
[PR815](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/815) studies frame
assignments of fixed scalar words. Here the scalar words and width inventory
change. This package adds four audited embeddings of PR781 and an exact
obstruction for their mixtures in PR626's budget; it makes no general novelty
claim for integer width prices or owner-packing methods.

The complete multiplication theorem retains its inherited all-size,
realization, hosting, precision/tape and analytic assumptions. This finite
certificate neither discharges those assumptions nor formally verifies the
full theorem. Attribution and licenses are recorded in [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md).
